title: Session 15 forgot
scenario: A team builds an internal web app with a long-running coding agent on the Claude Agent SDK. Each session is a fresh run of the agent. After three weeks the log looks bad (exhibit). A second team, which uses OpenAI models, also asks you which runtime to pick.
exhibit:
INSTRUCTION FILE (CLAUDE.md, excerpt)
  - Use 2-space indentation.
  - Never edit .env files.

HARNESS
  each session: same prompt "Keep building the app from the spec."
  no progress file, agent does not commit

INCIDENT LOG
  session 9   agent edited .env to change a port
  session 15  started a feature that session 14 had half built;
              no notes about session 14 anywhere
  session 22  agent: "The app is complete."
              QA: 61 of 200 spec features never tested, 18 broken

SECOND TEAM (OpenAI)
  needs: agent writes and runs scripts in a sandbox,
         vendor runs the loop, least code on their side

questions.prompt: The ".env" rule was in CLAUDE.md, but session 9 broke it. What change matches the Claude Code docs?

options.text: Write the rule in capital letters at the top of CLAUDE.md.
options.explanation: It is still an instruction the model reads. The docs call such a line a request, not a guarantee.

options.text: Move the rule into a skill so it loads when needed.
options.explanation: A skill is interpreted by Claude too, so its outcome can vary. It does not enforce anything.

options.text: Add a `PreToolUse` hook that blocks edits to `.env`.
options.explanation: Right. The docs: a `PreToolUse` hook that blocks the edit is enforcement. If a rule must hold every time, make it a hook.

options.text: Repeat the rule in every session's prompt as well.
options.explanation: Saying it twice is still a request. A hook always fires on its event; how the model follows an instruction can vary.

questions.prompt: Session 15 did not know what session 14 did. What did Anthropic's long-running harness add for this?

options.text: A progress file and git commits, read at the start of every session.
options.explanation: Right. Each session read the progress notes and git log first, and ended with a commit and a progress update.

options.text: A larger context window, so one session can hold all three weeks.
options.explanation: Each new session still begins with no memory of what came before. The state has to live outside the context.

options.text: Automatic compaction, which carries the old session into the new one.
options.explanation: The Anthropic engineering post says compaction is not sufficient here; it does not always pass perfectly clear instructions to the next agent.

options.text: A prompt that asks the agent to build the whole app in one session.
options.explanation: That was the failure Anthropic saw first: trying to do too much at once and running out of context mid-feature.

questions.prompt: In session 22 the agent declared the app complete too early. Which fix is from Anthropic's post?

options.text: A shorter session prompt, so the agent reads the spec faster and skips old notes.
options.explanation: The prompt length was not the issue. The agent had no clear list of what done means.

options.text: A feature list with every feature marked failing, passed only after testing.
options.explanation: Right. The initializer wrote over 200 features as failing; coding agents worked on one at a time and marked it passing only after careful testing.

options.text: Let the agent delete features it cannot finish from the spec to keep the list short.
options.explanation: The opposite: Anthropic told agents that removing or editing tests is unacceptable, because features would go missing.

options.text: Keep the spec in a Markdown file the agent may freely rewrite.
options.explanation: Anthropic used JSON because the model was less likely to change or overwrite JSON files than Markdown files.

questions.prompt: Which OpenAI option fits the second team's needs?

options.text: The Responses API, with their own loop built around it.
options.explanation: OpenAI rates that integration effort High: they would write the loop. The team wants the vendor to run it.

options.text: The Agents SDK, inside their own application.
options.explanation: The SDK runs in their app, so they still host and run the loop. OpenAI rates the effort Medium.
With no environment, the built-in Bash and apply-patch tools and workspace files are unavailable, so the agent can't run scripts.

options.text: The Agents API with an `openai_hosted` environment.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI runs the managed Codex harness, and an OpenAI-hosted environment gives the agent a sandbox to run scripts and edit files.
